summary: Rocket Lab has protested NASA's decision to award Blue Origin a $700 million Mars orbiter contract, even as the launch provider successfully placed a secret satellite into orbit for an undisclosed customer. In space technology, Antares secured a $161 million award for space nuclear power, while NASA and IBM released a new artificial intelligence model trained on 17 years of lunar data to boost open science under the Artemis Accords. Planetary science saw key milestones as Japan's Hayabusa2 achieved the first-ever laser ranging experiment with an asteroid, and researchers published a new surface atlas of Phobos to support sample-collection planning for the upcoming Martian Moons eXploration mission. On the defense and international front, the U.S. Space Force selected Texas as the domestic site for the trinational Deep Space Advanced Radar Capability network, the U.S. and allied partners agreed to update multinational secure communications agreements, and Poland announced plans to develop its own satellite internet constellation. In commercial operations, two private spacecraft demonstrated advanced proximity capabilities by maneuvering within 650 feet of each other in Earth orbit. Looking ahead, readers should watch for NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 astronauts to host a media briefing addressing their orbital mission and upcoming return to Earth.
